narrative.summary: ICESCO's AI instrument is the Riyadh Charter on Artificial Intelligence for the Islamic World (2025), developed with Saudi Arabia's SDAIA at the request of ICESCO's Executive Council. It sets ethical principles for the design, conduct and governance of AI grounded in Islamic values and recommends impact assessments, a trustworthy-AI label and national regulatory frameworks. ICESCO also runs a Center of Foresight and Artificial Intelligence.
lead_institutions: ICESCO Center of Foresight and Artificial Intelligence

The member list comes from ICESCO's member-states page, as the older isesco.org address no longer serves it. Observer states are not listed. instruments.current_status: Published by ICESCO in 2025 (only the year is printed) in cooperation with SDAIA; the text calls itself 'a shared vision, a declaration of intent, and a guiding compass'. Adopted by the ICESCO Executive Council at its 45th session (Tunis, 26 February 2025 as printed in the Report of the Executive Council to the General Conference; the session page gives 25-26 February 2025): Decision D.3.1 'Adopts the Riyadh Charter on Artificial Intelligence for the Islamic World-ICECSO' (sic), invites Member States to support it, and submits it to the General Conference with a recommendation for approval. The General Conference at its 15th session (Kazan, 13-14 May 2026) approved the decisions and recommendations of the Executive Council's 43rd, 44th, 45th and 46th sessions (Resolutions 2.1 and 4.1); no separate General Conference resolution on the Charter is printed in the Resolutions document.
instruments.summary: Ethical and strategic framework written as a declaration by the Governments of the Member States. It sets basic requirements and three groups of principles: ethical design (human dignity, personal sovereignty, truth and authenticity, solidarity, privacy, fairness and inclusion, well-being, trustworthiness), ethical conduct (prudence, responsibility) and ethical governance (human oversight, accountability, redress and compensation for harm), grounded in Islamic values. It makes recommendations to Member States and ICESCO across education, human and social sciences, science and technology, and culture and communication — including ex ante and ex post impact assessments, a quality label for education and culture applications, environmental impact assessment and capacity building — and closes with a strategic implementation roadmap including national AI readiness and impact assessment reports and an annual AI ministers' conference.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Ethical and strategic AI framework for the 53 ICESCO Member States.
metadata_gaps: Day of publication (only the year is printed on the Charter); General Conference approval is recorded only through the general approval of the 45th session decisions, not a Charter-specific resolution
